subject.title: fix(agents): avoid symlink-follow in auth.json bootstrap

question: After the async preserved-mode ordering bug is fixed, should no-final-path-chmod and exact-mode handling remain in OpenClaw's shared wrapper for this PR, or move into @openclaw/fs-safe first?
rationale: The diff changes a security-sensitive helper exported through the plugin SDK and used by auth/config/session paths, so automation can identify the correctness bug but cannot choose the permanent owner boundary for the dependency contract.

options.title: Fix Wrapper Then Secops Review
options.body: Repair the stale async mode lookup in this PR, keep the wrapper-level hardening, and merge only after secops accepts that ownership boundary.

options.title: Move Into fs-safe First
options.body: Patch or update @openclaw/fs-safe so the dependency primitive owns no-follow-safe exact mode handling, then thin OpenClaw's wrapper back down.

options.title: Narrow To Auth Bootstrap
options.body: Land only the auth.json bootstrap change and track shared atomic replacement hardening separately.

recommendation.title: Fix Wrapper Then Secops Review
recommendation.body: Repair the stale async mode lookup in this PR, keep the wrapper-level hardening, and merge only after secops accepts that ownership boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the listed Agents/Security routing owner, and this choice crosses the auth and security-helper boundary.
